speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination, have you noticed any burning sensation when you urinate, or any blood in your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the pain you feel in your bladder ever radiated to your lower back or abdomen, and have you noticed any changes in the color of your urine? Additionally, have you experienced any fever or chills recently?

speaker: Doctor
text: That response seems incomplete; did you mean to say the pain radiates during intercourse, or were you referring to a change in urine color? To help clarify the source of your discomfort, please tell me if you have noticed any blood in your urine or a foul odor. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Urine Culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Color: Clear, pH: 6.7, Specific_Gravity: 1.010, Protein: 1+, Glucose: Negative, Ketones: Negative, Blood: Negative, Nitrite: Negative, Leukocyte Esterase: Negative, WBC: 0/hpf, Squamous Epithelial Cells: 2/hpf, Bacteria: None

speaker: Doctor
text: The urinalysis shows no signs of infection, yet your symptoms of frequency and pain with intercourse are classic for interstitial cystitis. Have you noticed any cloudiness in the urine or recent onset of hematuria? REQUEST TEST: Cystoscopy to evaluate for Hunner's ulcers.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Cystoscopy: Normal urethra and bladder mucosa

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome.

Since your urinalysis and cystoscopy are normal, and your symptoms of chronic pelvic pain relieved by voiding, along with dyspareunia, are classic for this condition, I am confident in this diagnosis. We will begin treatment with a trial of bladder distension or oral pentosan polysulfate (Elmiron).
